description: The session scheduled for the evening of Nov 5 never ran overnight: the Mac entered clamshell sleep on battery shortly before the scheduled start and stayed asleep (maintenance dark wakes only) until the lid was opened the next morning. The scheduled task fired only after the full wake, past the five-in-the-morning cutoff, so no experiments were run. Nothing in the program can keep the machine awake from a closed-lid, on-battery sleep; it needs the lid open on AC power or a change to power settings, which is Chris's call.

Correction and resolution of B0001. Chris reported on Nov 6 that the Nov 5 session was missed mainly because of a permissions issue, which he has since fixed, not because of sleep as B0001 and that session's summary said; the Mac is now kept on AC with the lid open overnight.
resolution: Tonight's session (evening of Nov 6) fired at 23:07, on schedule, with the Mac on AC (pmset log: full wake at 22:45 from user activity, on AC). The earlier diagnosis blamed sleep alone; future misses will be checked against the task-run history and permission prompts as well as the power log.

description: The Mac entered 'Clamshell Sleep' (lid closed) at 23:57:32 on Nov 8, 34 minutes into the session, and stayed asleep apart from brief maintenance dark wakes (00:22:50 for 63 s, 00:29:42) until at least 00:32. Background jobs and the session paused; the session resumed in a dark wake at 00:29 and wrapped up early in case the machine slept again. The Mac had also rebooted at 23:23, before the scheduled 23:00 session began (it started at 23:26). caffeinate -i does not prevent clamshell sleep. Needs: the lid left open on AC overnight (or an external display), as in the Nov 6 setup.

Recurred on Nov 9: the Mac entered 'Clamshell Sleep' (lid closed) at 23:23:30, fifteen minutes into the session, and from then until at least 02:25 it had only maintenance dark wakes of about a minute every fifteen minutes. Background jobs got about twenty-five CPU-minutes each in three hours. The session resumed in a dark wake at about 02:15 and wrapped up early. caffeinate -i does not prevent clamshell sleep. Needs: the lid left open on AC overnight, or an external display attached.

Free disk fell below the 40 GB floor during the session, from causes outside the program. At the 23:08 start it was 43 GB (93 GB at the start of the Nov 9 session); by 23:11 it was 39.8 GB and by 23:18 35.8 GB. sequel-data is 2.6 GB of the 15 GB program budget and did not grow. The fall tracks swap: vm.swapusage went to 24.3 GB used of 25.6 GB, in 1 GB steps, while other work on the Mac (about fourteen Python workers from two Dogsled b2 worktrees, some at 1 to 2 GB resident each) was running; the load average was 115 to 138 at the start. The session did not touch those processes. Because the floor is an instant limit, the session launched no new simulations while below it: the remaining 15 engine-comparison runs (E0031) and all five E0034 runs wait in a queue (tools/qx3.sh) that launches only when free disk is at or above 40.5 GB. The three E0031 runs already running were left to finish (their output is a few MB).

Update at 23:31: free disk 23.8 GB and falling about 1.4 GB a minute; swap 36.8 GB used of 37.9 GB. The growth is in one job outside the program: review_salt_components.py (PID 79154, started about 22:35 from the Dogsled b2 worktree protonation-states-conflation) and its twelve workers, about 66 GB of memory in all at 23:23 with one worker at 23 GB, nearly all of it compressed or swapped. The session sent two desktop notifications (mobile push was not available) and did not stop the job, which is not the program's to touch. If the disk fills, the program's two running simulations will fail at their next checkpoint write; all records were committed at 23:25 (fa3ebf9).

Update at 23:52: free disk 7.6 GB, swap 55.2 GB used; the outside job (PID 79154) is still running. One program simulation is still running (E0031 main-g5-f0.5-d5-s3); the other reached its CPU cap. All queues remain held and will launch by themselves if free disk returns above 40.5 GB. Needs Chris: stop or fix the outside job and free the swap (a restart clears it).

Resolved: the outside job is gone and free disk was 65 GB at the 23:07 start of the Nov 11 session (63 GB at 01:15). Chris's Nov 11 instruction sets a hard floor of 25 GB for small runs when another job on the Mac is the cause; the queue (tools/qx4.sh) now holds launches only below 25.5 GB. The queues killed by the 00:05 crash on Nov 11 were restarted at 23:16.

description: The Mac's lid was closed at 23:26 on Nov 15, 19 minutes into the session, on AC power (pmset log: 'Clamshell Sleep' at 23:26:35 and 23:26:47; AppleClamshellState = Yes at 23:52). Since then the machine has run only in maintenance dark wakes: 21 seconds at 23:36 and one from 23:51:39. The session and both pilot ramps (E0058, E0059) are suspended between wakes: in the 41 minutes after launch the two ramps got about 17 and 13 CPU-minutes. caffeinate -i does not prevent clamshell sleep, and changing the system's sleep setting is not mine to do (Chris declined pmset disablesleep on Nov 6). The ramps are left running; they are checkpointed at every step, resumable, and will go on whenever the machine is awake. This is the same failure as B0002 (Nov 8 and 9). Needs Chris: open the lid (or attach a display) for overnight sessions. The two ramps then need about 7 more CPU-hours between them, at low priority.

Resolved: the lid was opened on the morning of Nov 16 and the two pilot ramps (E0058, E0059) finished that day. In the Nov 16 session the Mac was on AC power with the lid open (AppleClamshellState = No at 23:07) and the power log has no sleep or wake event from 22:55 on.
resolution: lid open on AC power for the whole Nov 16 session; no sleep events; the two suspended ramps finished
